Average Yields of Long-Term Treasury and Corporate Bonds

In response to requests for earlier figures on the average yields of long-term partially tax-exempt Treasury bonds and long-term high-grade corporate bonds, the following table and charts have been prepared to present monthly and weekly (Saturday) figures beginning with January 1933. Certain revisions in previously published data for recent periods are also incorporated.

The Treasury bond series consists of the average of partially tax-exempt Treasury bonds not due or callable for 12 years. Partially tax-exempt bonds are issues the income from which is exempt from the normal rates of the Federal income tax. (In the case of Treasury bonds with the partial tax-exemption privilege, interest derived from $5,000 of principal amount owned by any single holder is also exempt from the surtax rates of the Federal income tax.)

The corporate bond average consists currently of 5 long-term high-grade bonds. It is not possible at this time to obtain a broader list of corporate bonds upon which to base a satisfactory average because practically all actively traded high-grade callable bonds are now selling above their call prices, and because there are very few long-term high-grade non-callable bonds other than rails. In view of these difficulties, the Treasury corporate bond average, beginning with September 14, 1938, has been confined to a list of 5 bonds which are actually "free" to move and so indicate changes in the underlying market. The number of bonds will be increased at some future date when additional issues suitable for inclusion in the index are available.

As of July 1, 1941, the list of bonds was revised, and now includes the following issues:
Norfolk and Western Railway Company 4 1/8's of 1996
New England Telephone and Telegraph Company 4-1/2's of 1961
Bell Telephone Company of Pennsylvania 5's of 1960
Boston Edison Company 2-3/4's of 1970
Illinois Bell Telephone Company 2-3/4's of 1981
The average yield of the 5 bonds now included in the index was 2.65 percent on July 1. As of the same date the average yield of the bonds previously included was 2.66 percent. The continuity of the index was not, therefore, substantially impaired by the revision. The same was true in the case of prior revisions of the index.

Monthly yields for the Treasury bond series are averages of daily yields. Monthly yields for the corporate bond series are averages of daily yields beginning with April 1938; for prior months they are averages of Saturday figures.

Monthly figures for Treasury bonds earlier than 1933 may be found in the "Annual Report of the Secretary of the Treasury for 1939"; weekly figures may be found in a mimeographed statement presenting daily figures which is available from the Treasury Department, Division of Research and Statistics. Figures for high-grade corporate bonds are not available for periods prior to 1933.

As has been the practice, daily figures are presented for a period of six weeks. Back daily figures are available in previous issues of the "Treasury Bulletin" and in the mimeographed statement referred to above.
